diagnosis.cause: Kane fails because a valid submit only shows a short-lived toast and leaves the form in place, matching the failing remark: “The booking form stayed on screen after the user submitted valid visit details, rather than completing the booking and displaying its confirmation.”
patterns: Ambiguous duplicate call-to-action labels: both hero and nav buttons say “Go”, and the nav “Go” opens prices instead of the booking form.
Blocking cookie overlay has a tiny “x” close control implemented as a div, not a labelled real button.
Booking fields are identified only by placeholders, with no associated visible labels.
Date format is not disclosed, and validation reports only the generic message “Invalid input”.
Arrival time and waiver are custom div-based controls rather than native radio/checkbox controls.
Success feedback is a transient toast that disappears after 2.5 seconds instead of a persistent, announced confirmation containing the reference.
changes: Replace the cookie close div `#cookie-close` with a real `<button type="button">` labelled clearly, e.g. `aria-label="Close cookie notice"`, while preserving the same small visual style.
Change the ambiguous CTA button text: make `#hero-go` and `#nav-go` say “Book free visit” or similar, and wire both to `openBooking()` so neither leads to the prices dead end.

Add visible `<label for="name">Your name</label>`, `<label for="email">Email address</label>`, and `<label for="date">Visit date</label>` above the existing inputs; set useful input types such as `type="email"` and `type="date"`.

Add helper text for the date field, e.g. “Use YYYY-MM-DD”, if keeping the text input fallback; replace the generic `Invalid input` error with a specific message that names missing/invalid name, email, date, arrival time, or waiver acceptance.

Replace the custom arrival time divs with a native radio group using three `<input type="radio" name="time" value="09:00|12:00|18:00">` options labelled 9am, 12pm, and 6pm, styled to preserve the existing time-slot look.
Replace the custom waiver div with a native `<input type="checkbox" id="waiver" name="waiver">` and associated label text “I accept the climbing waiver.”

Add a persistent confirmation area inside or immediately after `#booking`, e.g. `
`, containing copy that confirms the free first visit and includes `PL-4821`.

On valid submit, hide or disable the form, reveal the persistent `#confirmation`, and keep `PL-4821` visible for at least five seconds; simplest and safest is to not auto-hide it at all. The existing toast may be removed or left secondary, but it must not be the only success state.
diagnosis.acceptanceCheck: A fresh Kane run can close the cookie notice, open the booking from either main CTA, fill Sam Rivera / sam@example.com / 2026-11-02, choose noon, accept the waiver, submit, and observe a persistent booking confirmation containing `PL-4821`; after waiting five seconds, `PL-4821` is still visible on the page.
